messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — onboarding llama-3-16k q8 into eu-west. We see p95 latency: vendor-lib (nv-infer) ~18ms, flashv3/triton ~26ms. BUT evals show a ~7% drop in answer-ranking on our instr-follow suite vs fp16. Thoughts on switching kernels regionally vs forcing flashv3 for quality?
jonathan: Can you paste the payload distribution and batch sizes? also exact quant config (q8 symmetric/affine/hybrid)?
maya: payloads skew short — 72% <256 tokens, median 120. Batching mostly 1-4. Quant: q8_dynamic with per-tensor scales (default toolchain) — no outlier handling.
samir: that pattern fits a numeric stability issue in the vendor kernels for small seqs. flashv2 historically was more stable on short context but slower. flashv3 improves perf but vendor lib still wins latency.
rachel: For production SLOs we care quality > latency for this model. Options: 1) route eu-west to flashv3 for all requests (preserve quality, cost higher), 2) hybrid routing by payload shape, 3) fix quant config (q8_hybrid / per-channel) and re-eval. I'm leaning to (2) short-term + (3) medium-term.
maya: +1. Hybrid would keep user latency wins for long-form while protecting instruction accuracy on short queries. Any safe routing policy suggestion?
rachel: Something like:
```
route: 
  - if region == "eu-west" and seq_len <= 256: use flashv3
  - else if region == "eu-west" and seq_len > 256: use vendor-infer
  - fallback: flashv3
canary: 10% traffic to vendor-infer for seq>256
metrics: eval.rank, latency.p95, error.rate
```
samir: Also add a quality probe: run the small-instr eval on a sampled 0.1% live requests (deterministic prompts) and failover if rank drops >3% over 1h.
 e.g.
```
probe: sample(0.1%) -> run_eval(instrumented_prompts) -> if delta_rank > 0.03 rollback_to flashv3
```
 evaluator: FWIW I ran the offline eval with q8_hybrid (per-channel for attention weights) — rank drop reduced to ~1.5% and p95 goes up to 20ms (still better than flashv3). Patch attached: `eval/llama3/q8_hybrid/eu-west/2026-03-19.log`
maya: Nice. So plan: 1) deploy q8_hybrid build to canary in eu-west (10%) 2) if offline eval looks good, flip routing for seq<=256 to q8_hybrid vendor-lib 3) keep flashv3 as failback and long-form default.
deploy-bot: Canary starts: `canary/llama3-q8-hybrid` -> eu-west -> 10% traffic. Tags: canary-20260319, owner=maya.
jonathan: Reminder: check GPU kernels for microburst warmup — vendor lib sometimes shows jit-like slowdowns on sudden spikes. Add warmup policy: prebuffer 10s during scale-up.
samir: also add `numeric-check` traces for a small subset to capture divergences.
maya: I'll run the numeric traces + schedule the canary and re-run the full eval after 4h. Will post results here. :thumbsup:
